question: When reserving a campsite with Parks Canada, does the reservation automatically give me a national park admission pass?
generated_answer:
No, a campsite reservation does not automatically include a national park admission pass. However, if you purchase a Discovery Pass, you will receive a paper pass that you can show at the park entrance to gain admission to the park. Alternatively, you can purchase a digital park pass that is linked to your reservation, but this requires an active cell signal or data plan at the park entrance to access the digital pass. Always check with Parks Canada or the specific park for the most up-to-date information on admission passes and how to use them.

It is important to note that while some national parks may offer free admission or free days, not all parks offer this, and some may require a pass for entry. Therefore, it is always best to plan ahead and check the specific requirements for the park you will be visiting.

Additionally, if you have a reservation for a campsite in a national park, you may be required to show proof of reservation at the park entrance, even if you have a park pass. So, it is a good idea to have your reservation confirmation handy.

In summary, while a campsite reservation does not automatically give you a national park admission pass, you can purchase a pass separately or link it to your reservation in some cases. Always check with Parks Canada or the specific park for the most up-to-date information and requirements.
